records.quote: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids) examines the burning and extinction characteristics of a wide variety of fuel samples in microgravity.
records.derivation: Investigation-level description in the PSI Data Layout Document; the sentence spans two PDF lines (joined with one space).

records.test_id: 1-11 (cotton-fiberglass fabric tests; numbering of Table I in the 2013 paper)
records.quote: Microgravity combustion tests burning fabric samples were performed aboard the International Space Station.
records.derivation: First sentence of the abstract. Scope is the fabric tests of this paper; the paper's test numbers may not match the PSI test numbering.

records.test_id: 1-g upward (concurrent) comparison flame, no test number given (Fig. 13 of the 2013 paper)
records.quote: In Fig. 13, a comparison is made for two flames burning in concurrent flow, but with one in microgravity and the other in normal gravity.
records.derivation: 1-g comparison flame reported alongside the flight tests. The paper gives no test number and does not say where it was run. Figure 13 caption (paragraph 180): 'Comparison of 0-g concurrent-flow flame (left) and 1-g upward flame (right) for 2-cm wide sample.'

records.test_id: 1-g opposed-flow (downward) comparison flame, no test number given (Fig. 14 of the 2013 paper)
records.quote: Figure 14.  Comparison of 0-g and 1-g flames in opposed flow.  Image sequences shows flames spreading from top down.  (Test 6 and a 1-g test)
records.derivation: Figure caption (double spaces as in the document). 'Test 6' is the 0-g flight test; the 1-g test has no number and the paper does not say where it was run. Paragraph 179 adds: 'On the right, the normal-gravity, downward-burning flame is ignited, but sputters and then goes out.'
Investigation title (a name, not a sentence). See R6 for the requirement sentence.

records.quote: Configuration: Solid fuel materials on individual and exchangeable sample cards
records.derivation: 'BASS Requirement' column of the requirements table, row 'Configuration' (planning document, February 2010). Note for the auditor: SRD page 4, Figure 1 labels the sample 'Solid fuel or wax-impregnated “wick”', and the test matrix (page 10) includes wax candles and wax-saturated fabric; the sources do not state a phase for the wax samples separately.

records.quote: The experiment was conducted aboard the International Space Station (ISS) inside the Microgravity Glove Box (MSG).
records.derivation: Vehicle. Section=flightProgram also reads 'International Space Station (ISS)'.
Facility (field value, not a sentence). Section=approach writes it 'Microgravity Glove Box (MSG)'; the 2013 paper, paragraph 53, writes 'Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)'.

records.quote: The air co-flow is produced by using a fan to blow air through the duct.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. The 2013 paper (paragraph 51) also speaks of 'air flow speeds'. Separate note, NOT the ambient diluent: the extinguishing agent is nitrogen, SRD page 4: '3.) Nitrogen gas jet for flame extinguishment'; record section=researchImpacts: 'Using nitrogen as a flame suppressant in microgravity provides a direct link to current and planned extinguishment techniques.'

records.quote: This investigation explored two primary air flow configurations; concurrent-flow and opposed-flow. With concurrent-flow air flows in the same direction as the flame spread and in opposed-flow air flows in the opposite direction of flame spread.
records.derivation: Investigation-level statement that both configurations were used; it does not say which test used which, so this value does not hold for every test. Per-test directions for the fabric tests are in Table I of the 2013 paper (paragraphs 79-142, paper numbering). Nothing is stated for the spheres or candles.

records.quote: This investigation explored two primary air flow configurations; concurrent-flow and opposed-flow. With concurrent-flow air flows in the same direction as the flame spread and in opposed-flow air flows in the opposite direction of flame spread.
records.derivation: Same sentence as R10: both configurations were used; it does not say which test used which. Per-test directions for the fabric tests are in Table I of the 2013 paper (paragraphs 79-142, paper numbering).

records.quote: The air co-flow is produced by using a fan to blow air through the duct.
records.derivation: Planning document (February 2010). 'co-flow' is the name of the duct air stream carried over from SPICE (SRD page 7, SPICE column: 'Configuration: Round gas jet diffusion flame in a co-flowing oxidizer stream'); it may name the duct stream rather than the flame/flow configuration. The PSI record describes the configurations as concurrent or opposed (R10, R11). Not assigned to specific tests.

records.quote: Airflow was controlled using a variable speed fan, with airflow speeds reaching as high as 40 cm/s.
records.derivation: Upper bound only ('as high as'); the sentence gives no lower bound. Agrees with the 40 cm/s maximum in R14; disagrees with the 5 to 50 cm/s of the planning SRD (R15).

records.test_id: 1-11 (cotton-fiberglass fabric tests; numbering of Table I in the 2013 paper)
records.quote: A variable-speed fan is used to generate air flow speeds from 0 to 40 cm/s.
records.derivation: Hardware range from the paper's Methods; the abstract (paragraph 17) says 'up to 40 cm/s'. Note for the auditor: the paper's own Table I lists 44 cm/s for two tests (paragraphs 126 and 131), above this stated maximum, and paragraph 75 says 'The minimum measurable air flow speed is 1 cm/s.' Disagrees with the 5 to 50 cm/s of the planning SRD (R15).

records.quote: An anemometer is used to measure the actual flow speed. The airflow speed can be adjusted from 5 to 50 cm/s.
records.derivation: Planning document (Science Requirements, February 2010) describing the existing SPICE fan and duct. SRD page 7 repeats 'Oxidizer Velocity: 5 to 50 cm/s' and 'Co-flow Velocity: 5 to 50 cm/s', with the BASS column '---Same---' as SPICE. Disagrees with the 0 to 40 cm/s of R13 and R14.

records.quote: On each day of testing, the oxygen concentration of the ISS cabin atmosphere should be measured. Testing is restricted to oxygen concentrations at or above 21% O2.
records.derivation: Lower bound only, and a requirement in the February 2010 planning SRD ('Ambient Oxygen Concentration Requirements', BASS column), not a measured value. The same restriction is repeated on page 8 for the MSG working volume. The as-run O2 is not stated in the record text or the 2013 paper. The percent basis (volume/mole or mass) is not stated. The '2' in 'O2' is a subscript in the PDF.

records.quote: A snapshot of 2-cm diameter acrylic sphere burning in microgravity at 17 percent oxygen and 10 cm/s flow from the Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) experiment conducted on the International Space Station.
records.derivation: Figure caption in the 2015 ISS Researcher's Guide describing an actual BASS test (acrylic sphere, 17 % O2, 10 cm/s) 'conducted on the International Space Station'.

records.quote: Recent results from the BASS experiment currently running on the ISS indicate that NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative, and materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.
records.derivation: Results sentence about the BASS experiment in the 2015 ISS Researcher's Guide; it states the microgravity comparison without naming individual tests.

not_found.looked_in: record text (all sections), SRD pages 1-11, 2013 paper (all paragraphs), DLD page 1. No numeric value anywhere. The only mention is the SRD page 7 requirements table: SPICE column 'Pressure: Shuttle ambient pressure', BASS column '---Same---' (a term inherited from SPICE, no number, and written for the Shuttle although BASS ran on the ISS).
record text (all sections), 2013 paper (all paragraphs), DLD page 1. Only the SRD lower-bound requirement exists (R16).

lineage: SPICE hardware is stated: SRD page 1 'An ISS Glovebox Experiment Utilizing Existing SPICE Hardware with Minor Modifications'; SRD page 4 'The plan is to use the existing NASA glovebox SPICE hardware with four changes:'; 2013 paper paragraph 51 'The samples are burned in the SPICE apparatus which is a small flow duct with a cross-sectional area of 76mm x 76mm [Dotson et. al. 2010].' The cotton-fiberglass fuel is the SIBAL fabric (SRD page 5, footnote 1: 'Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low Speed (Principal Investigator: James T’ien) was a previously funded flight project [...]'). BASS-II and SLICE are not mentioned in any source read.
